transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 mins
- Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO), Dana (ML Eng), Sam (Infra)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on latency and throughput requirements for Constellation Payments' fraud-detection and realtime-risk pipeline. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) deployment for p95 latency targets and token/sec throughput; wants streaming and high concurrency support. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run benchmarks and share security docs + pricing; customer to share detailed traffic profile.

Transcript:
[00:00] Morgan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Morgan, AE, with Priya our systems SE. Quick intros?
[00:15] Alex (Constellation): Alex here, CTO, running payments stack. Dana is our ML lead and Sam runs infra. We're mainly interested in embedding/rerank + chat gen for realtime risk scoring.
[00:32] Priya (Redwood): Great. High level - we support hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency. Today want to focus on p95 latency and concurrency right?
[00:45] Alex: Yeah p95 under 120ms for short prompts would be ideal for scoring use case, but we also have burst concurrency up to ~1k qps across geos. Main question is whether hosted can meet p95 at that scale or we need Dedicated.
[01:05] Dana: Also streaming is important — we need partial tokens quickly to feed our risk worker. Token/sec throughput matters; we're estimating 5000 tokens/sec sustained per region during peaks.
[01:20] Priya: Cool. Couple clarifying q's: what model families are you aiming for? open weights or commercial? and sequence lengths — avg and 95th?
[01:35] Alex: We'll be on an open model family, 4k-8k context variants, avg prompt+response ~600 tokens, p95 ~2.5k tokens. We're okay with 8-bit quantized models if quality holds.
[01:50] Sam: Security is non-negotiable - SOC2, customer-managed KMS (HSM) for keys, VPC peering. Audit logs and RBAC.
[02:05] Morgan: All standard asks. We have SOC2 docs and KMS integrations; Dedicated and Private support customer KMS and audit logs. We'll include those in the security pack.
[02:18] Priya: For latency - short answer is it depends on model, hardware, batch policy, and KV cache behavior. For hosted, our verified configs hit p95 ~80-150ms for 2-4k context on optimized models under typical load; Dedicated gives tighter SLOs because you get reserved GPU pools and can tune batching aggressively.
[02:42] Dana: Can you give a ballpark for tokens/sec per GPU? we have some internal numbers but want Redwood-specific guidance.
[02:52] Priya: Ballpark: on an A100-like profile with optimized kernels, expect ~1.2k-2.5k tokens/sec for 4k context depending on quant and model. With L4-like newer hardware or multi-GPU sharding, you can push much higher. These are noisy numbers — we'll run your exact model and prompt mix.
[03:12] Alex: For p95 we care more about tail than average. If we get spikes, can Redwood fallback to smaller variants or region-level routing?
[03:22] Morgan: Yes — smart routing can fallback to cheaper variants or different regions. We also have automatic fallback policies to maintain availability. Canary and A/B rollouts supported too.
[03:34] Sam: On Dedicated, what isolation do we get? can we control autoscale thresholds, and burst capacity?
[03:42] Priya: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools. You can configure autoscale policies and burst to shared capacity; SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers available on enterprise plans.
[03:54] Dana: What's the typical p95 delta between hosted and dedicated? like numbers in ms?
[04:00] Priya: Typically hosted p95 for optimized models is 80-200ms for short prompts; Dedicated we commonly see 60-140ms because of predictable batching and no noisy neighbors. But real numbers depend on concurrency and streaming patterns.
[04:18] Alex: For streaming: does Redwood support partial token streaming within 30-50ms? we need something that can push first tokens quickly so our workers can start scoring.
[04:30] Priya: Yes streaming supported. First token latency will be dominated by decode step and model init; on tuned stacks we hit first token around ~40-120ms on common configs. We'll validate with your prompt set.
[04:50] Morgan: Let's talk benchmarks — best practice is to run token/sec and p95 tests with your actual prompts, target concurrency slabs, and context length. We'll provision a short benchmark harness on Dedicated and hosted to compare.
[05:05] Dana: Good. Our target p95 is 120ms for 600-token average and 2.5k for tail. Concurrent sessions at peak 1k qps across 3 regions, with per-user streaming.
[05:20] Priya: That profile is helpful. We'll run tests at 200/500/1k concurrency levels and measure p50/p90/p95 and tokens/sec, plus memory/KV cache hit rates. We'll also capture metrics like latency breakdown per token, batching factor, and queuing time.
[05:38] Alex: If Dedicated is needed, what's the procurement lead time?
[05:42] Morgan: Typically Dedicated onboarding is 2-6 weeks depending on contract and infra (VPC peering, KMS). Private on-prem takes longer; VPC can be quicker if your cloud accounts already set.
[05:55] Sam: Any known gotchas with KV cache or streaming that impacts tail latency?
[06:00] Priya: KV cache warms matter — if you have many cold prefixes you'll see higher latency. We do continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce cost and tail. Also tokenization variance matters. We'll instrument and recommend quantization profiles.
[06:16] Dana: On quantization: if we go 4-bit/8-bit, how often do you see quality regressions?
[06:22] Priya: It varies by model. We provide recommendations and quality monitoring; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles by workload and detect regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
[06:35] Alex: Compliance question — can logs be exported to our SIEM and do you support per-request PII redaction?
[06:42] Morgan: Yes audit logs and streaming logs can be exported; we have masking/redaction patterns and integrations with common SIEMs. We'll include details in the security pack.
[06:55] Priya: Regarding pricing tradeoffs: hosted is usage-based so burst friendly but potentially less predictable; Dedicated is commit-based and more economical at scale. We'll send a comparison.
[07:10] Alex: Competitors we've looked at include Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints; also evaluating running our own inference. Key tie-breakers are predictable p95 and SSO/KMS compliance.
[07:24] Morgan: Makes sense.
[07:28] Dana: For the benchmark, can Redwood run both hosted and dedicated runs with identical load generator so we can compare?
[07:36] Priya: Yes we'll run identical harness and share raw logs. We'll also capture token/sec and GPU utilization. Expect initial results within ~3 business days after we get your prompt set.
[07:50] Alex: Networking: VPC peering for Dedicated — is egress charged separately?
[07:55] Morgan: Egress depends on cloud provider; we'll include networking notes in the deployment doc. Private on-prem avoids cloud egress.
[08:06] Sam: Any limits on concurrent streaming connections? we plan to open persistent WS per user.
[08:12] Priya: No hard limit but concurrent connections factor into capacity planning; Dedicated gives you reserved headroom.
[08:22] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps.
[08:24] Morgan: Redwood will: 1) send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM notes, audit log export docs) 2) send hosted vs dedicated pricing and SLA samples 3) SE run benchmark (200/500/1k concurrency, token/sec, p95) using customer's prompt set 4) schedule follow-up in ~1 week to review results.
[08:45] Alex: We'll provide the prompt set and traffic profile by Friday, plus confirmation on model variant.
[08:52] Dana: One more - can you include recommendations about batching configs and quant profiles in the report?
[08:58] Priya: Yep, we'll include batching/caching config suggestions and quality notes from Redwood Optimize.
[09:05] Morgan: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and benchmark dates.
